## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag breaks the project's CLI-flag rule because it does not take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, so CI cannot set it. Fix that before merge. The exclusion logic itself is covered by tests at the `collect` and `main` levels.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py`. `collect` now skips any file whose basename matches one of the patterns and logs each skipped file. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests, and adds a one-line text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, `.log` files are still archived, because the flag is declared with `default=[]` and never reads the environment. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot use exclusions, and the new flag breaks the project's flag contract. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, splitting it on a documented separator such as `os.pathsep`, add the variable to `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
